pairs.subject: visual-script-to-code-transpilation
pairs.evidence: src/lib/blueprint-cpp-codegen.ts:105 The Blueprint-to-C++ codegen derives class members from a CppSurface model that restricts event overrides to three non-ancestral engine callbacks and maps types without totality.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/blueprint-cpp-surface.ts:61 Event override resolution is hardcoded to three engine events using a boolean component flag rather than walking the owner ancestry.
src/lib/blueprint-parser.ts:64 Execution control pins are mapped directly to void in the value type map, and unmapped types fall back to string literals instead of an explicit total representation.
src/lib/blueprint-semantic-diff.ts:48 The semantic diff explicitly skips function bodies and event graph node logic, bounding verification to declared member signatures.
src/lib/blueprint-jargon.ts:35 The jargon glossary provides one-sentence, consequence-oriented explanations for engine specifiers and graph node types across designer and engineer audiences.
src/__tests__/lib/blueprint-cpp-surface.test.ts:79 Parity verification only re-parses the emitted C++ header artifact, leaving parity with the emitted source definitions unchecked by parsers.

declined.subject: visual-script-to-code-transpilation
declined.reason: Visual ability-spec editor and GUI code generator, not a visual script transpiler. Per standard (lines 141-145), generating engine code from written specifications lacks a source graph to diff against and belongs to spec codegen rather than visual script transpilation.
